l402_spec_reference: lightninglabs/L402 protocol-specification.md + macaroon-spec.md. One correction applied against macaroon-spec.md's documented HMAC chain, verified against pymacaroons (the spec's own named Python reference implementation): the real chain derives a key first -- derived_key = HMAC-SHA256(b'macaroons-key-generator', root_key), sig_0 = HMAC-SHA256(derived_key, identifier) -- which the doc's sig_0 = HMAC(root_key, identifier) formula omits. A macaroon minted per the doc's literal formula would not verify against pymacaroons, libmacaroons, or gopkg.in/macaroon.v2 (so not against Aperture either). See PROVENANCE.md.
provenance: REAL, not synthetic. l402/server.py is a real, spec-faithful L402 server; its merchant invoice was created by a real phoenixd (ACINQ) testnet3 node. l402/client.py's payer is a separate real phoenixd testnet3 node, funded from a public testnet3 faucet, which paid that invoice over the real Lightning Network. The preimage above is this run's literal payment proof: sha256(preimage) == payment_hash, independently checked before being written here, and the server's own macaroon+preimage verification returned HTTP 200 for it. Aperture (lightninglabs' reference L402 proxy) was not run -- its lndclient backend does not support phoenixd, a different Lightning implementation. See PROVENANCE.md for the full statement, including why phoenixd and testnet3 (not Wavelength's own waved/Ark stack or signet).
